explanation: King Solomon was the son of King David and Bathsheba, known for his wisdom and as the builder of the first temple in Jerusalem.
A sacred building dedicated to God, where the Israelites worshipped and offered sacrifices. Solomon's Temple was the first temple in Jerusalem.
A large bronze basin in the temple, used by the priests for ritual cleansing before they performed their duties.
Two large bronze pillars, called Jachin and Boaz, which stood at the entrance to the temple as symbols of stability and strength.
A structure where burnt offerings and other sacrifices were presented to God as part of worship.
Candleholders used in the temple to provide light and symbolize God's presence.
Tables in the temple where the showbread was placed as a symbol of God's eternal presence and care for his people.
Bread that was placed on the tables in the temple as an offering and a symbol of God's presence and care for his people.
An altar in the temple where incense was burned as part of worship and to symbolize the prayers of the believers rising up to God.
